Rashi on Yevamot 7a:10:1.hebrew: בכלל כל הקדשים היו - שכבר כלל כרת בכולן: ״כל איש אשר יקרב מכל זרעכם אל הקדשים אשר יקדישו וגו'״:
Rashi on Yevamot 7a:10:1.english: Were included in all consecrated offerings - For [Scripture] had already included karet for all of them: “Any man of all your offspring who approaches the consecrated offerings that [the children of Israel] consecrate, etc.” (Leviticus 22:3).

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:10:2.english: And why were they singled out - In this verse a second time.

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:10:3.hebrew: יצאו קדשי בדק הבית - שאם אכלן בטומאת הגוף, פטור:
Rashi on Yevamot 7a:10:3.english: Excluded are consecrations for Temple maintenance - That if one ate them while in [a state of] bodily impurity, he is exempt [from karet].

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:11:1.english: Why was she singled out - [In the verse:] “Her brother-in-law shall have relations with her” [Deuteronomy 25:5].

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:12:1.english: Is it comparable? There, the generalization [is] in prohibition, etc. - There is room to state: "Why was it singled out?"

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:12:2.hebrew: הכא פרט בהיתר וכלל באיסור - ולאו להך דרשא דמי, דהא בדבר החדש יצא לידון:
Rashi on Yevamot 7a:12:2.english: Here the detail is in permission and the generalization is in prohibition - And it is not comparable to that exposition, for behold, it was singled out to be judged regarding a novel matter.

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:13:1.hebrew: אלא - להך דרשא: דבר שהיה בכלל, ויצא לידון בדבר החדש:
Rashi on Yevamot 7a:13:1.english: Rather - [It is comparable] to this exposition: “A matter that was included in a generalization but emerged to discuss a new matter.”

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:13:2.hebrew: אי אתה יכול להחזירו - ולהשוותו לכללו, ולא להשוות כללו לו:
Rashi on Yevamot 7a:13:2.english: You cannot return it - [Neither] to equate it with its generalization, nor to equate its generalization with it.

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:13:3.hebrew: עד שיחזירנו לך הכתוב - הילכך, בלאו עליה נמי לא אתי לן שאר עריות לייבום:
Rashi on Yevamot 7a:13:3.english: Until Scripture returns it to you - Therefore, even without [the verse] “aleha,” the other forbidden relatives would not be derived for us for levirate marriage either.

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:14:1.english: And he shall slaughter the sheep - It is written regarding the guilt-offering of a leper.

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:14:2.hebrew: כי כחטאת האשם הוא - כדין החטאת, כך דין אשם זה:
Rashi on Yevamot 7a:14:2.english: For as the sin-offering, [so] is the guilt-offering - As [is] the law of the sin-offering, so [is] the law of this guilt-offering.

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:14:3.hebrew: שאין ת"ל כחטאת - דהא אשם זה, אם לשחיטה בצפון, הלא כבר נאמר בו: ״ושחט את הכבש במקום אשר ישחט את החטאת״, ואם למתן דמים ואכילתו, הרי הוא ככל אשמות בכלל ״זאת תורת האשם״ בצו את אהרן:
Rashi on Yevamot 7a:14:3.english: As there is no need for the verse to state: “As the sin-offering” - For this guilt-offering, if [it is] for slaughter in the north, is it not already stated regarding it: “And he shall slaughter the sheep in the place where they slaughter the sin-offering” (Leviticus 14:13)? And if [it is] for the application of [its] blood and its eating, behold, it is like all guilt-offerings in the generalization: “This is the law of the guilt-offering” (Leviticus 7:1) in [Parashat] Tzav et Aharon.

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:15:1.english: Since the guilt-offering of a leper was singled out - From the general category of other guilt-offerings.

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:15:2.hebrew: לידון בדבר החדש - שאינו בשאר אשמות, בבהן יד ובבהן רגל. והואיל ויצא מכללו, יכול לא יהא טעון מתן דמים ואימורים לגבי מזבח — ת"ל כו':
Rashi on Yevamot 7a:15:2.english: To discuss a new matter - Which does not apply to other guilt-offerings: [namely,] on the thumb of the hand and on the big toe of the foot. And since it departed from its general category, [one] might [think that] it should not require the placement of blood and sacrificial parts on the altar — [therefore] the verse states, etc.

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:1:1.hebrew: רציחה דוחה אותה - שאם היה רוצח כהן ורוצה לעבוד עבודה, ב"ד שולחים ומביאין אותו למות, אלא א"כ היה על גגו של מזבח ועבודה בידו:
Rashi on Yevamot 7a:1:1.english: Murder overrides it - For if a murderer was a priest and wants to perform the [Temple] service, the court sends and brings him to die, unless he was on top of the altar and the service was in his hand.

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:1:2.english: As it is stated: “From beside My altar you shall take him to die” - But not from upon My altar.

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:2:1.hebrew: ומאי או אינו דקאמר - הואיל ומקל וחומר אתיא דדחיא, היכי מצינו למימר: או אינו אלא אפי' מיתת ב"ד לא דחיא:
Rashi on Yevamot 7a:2:1.english: And what is [the meaning of] “Or is it not” that it states - Since it is derived from an a fortiori inference that it overrides [Shabbat], how can we say: “Or is it not [the case, but] rather even court-imposed execution does not override [Shabbat]”?

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:2:2.hebrew: קבורת מת מצוה - דחיא עבודה — מולאחותו בפ"ק דמגילה (דף ג:) — ואינו דוחה את השבת. אף אני אביא רציחה, דאף על פי שדוחה עבודה, לא תדחה שבת. והאי דהדר אמר ״או אינו אלא אפילו בשבת״ — הכי הדר ואמר: קבורת מת מצוה גופה תדחה שבת, כו':
Rashi on Yevamot 7a:2:2.english: The burial of a met mitzva - Overrides the [Temple] service, [as derived] from “or for his sister” in the first chapter of Megillah (daf 3b), and yet it does not override Shabbat; so too, I will bring [the case of] murder, that even though it overrides the [Temple] service, it shall not override Shabbat. And that which [the tanna] then stated: “Or [is it] not [so], but rather even on Shabbat [it should override]?” — this is what he then stated: [Let] the burial of a met mitzva itself override Shabbat, etc.

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:4:1.hebrew: ולמאי דסליק אדעתיה למימר מעיקרא - דהאי דאיצטריך ליה קרא, משום דאי לא כתביה, ה"א אתי עשה ודחי לא תעשה:
Rashi on Yevamot 7a:4:1.english: And according to that which entered his mind to say at the outset - That [the reason] the verse was necessary for him [was] because had it not written it, I would have said [that] a positive commandment comes and overrides a negative commandment.

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:4:2.hebrew: מאי או אינו - היכי מצי למימר ״או אינו״, דלא דחי? במאי תיתי לן דלא תדחה:
Rashi on Yevamot 7a:4:2.english: What is [the meaning of] "Or perhaps not" - How could he say "Or perhaps not," that it does not override [Shabbat]? On what basis would it occur to us that it should not override [it]?

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:6:1.hebrew: אימור דאמרינן כו' - היינו דהדר ואמר: או אינו אלא אפי' במיתת ב"ד לא תדחי לאו דשבת, שהרי יש בו כרת:
Rashi on Yevamot 7a:6:1.english: Say that we said, etc. - This is [the meaning of that which] he then retracted and said: “Or is it not rather [that] even for court-imposed capital punishment, [a positive mitzva] should not override the prohibition of Shabbat, because it involves karet?”

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:6:2.english: He then retracted and said: Is that to say a positive commandment overrides, etc. - This is that which [the tanna] retracted and said: “Or is it rather even on Shabbat?”

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:6:3.english: Is not a prohibition more stringent than it - For one is lashed for it.

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:8:1.hebrew: אלא סלקא דעתך - לעיל קאי, דאוקימנא דהא דאיצטריך לא תבערו, משום דאי לא כתב רחמנא הוה מייתינן בק"ו, ולאו משום דאתי עשה ודחי ל"ת דכרת. ועליה למה לי? אלא, סד"א כו':
Rashi on Yevamot 7a:8:1.english: Rather, it could enter your mind - [This] refers back to above, where we established that [the reason] “You shall not kindle” was necessary was because had the Merciful One not written [it], we would have derived [it] by an a fortiori inference, and not because a positive commandment comes and overrides a negative commandment [punishable by] karet; and [if so,] why do I need “upon her”? Rather, it could enter your mind to say, etc.

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:8:2.hebrew: שהיה בכלל - כי כל אשר יעשה מכל התועבות האלה ונכרתו — כלל בכל העריות כרת:
Rashi on Yevamot 7a:8:2.english: That was included in the generalization - “For whoever does any of these abominations, [they] shall be cut off” — [this verse] generalized karet for all the forbidden relations.

Rashi on Yevamot 7a:8:3.english: And emerged from the generalization to teach - That if she has no children, she shall enter into levirate marriage.

Tosafot on Yevamot 7a:15:1.hebrew: לפי שיצא אשם מצורע לידון בדבר החדש - מה שחטאת מצורע טעונה נסכים, ושאר חטאות אין טעונות — לא חשיב דבר חדש. ואין קרוי דבר חדש אלא כשסותר כללו, כי הכא: דשאר אשמות טעונות כל הדם לגבי מזבח, ואשם מצורע נותן ממנו לבהונות; וכגון אשת אח: שנאסרו כל העריות, וזו הותרה — שסותר כללו. אבל מה שחטאת מצורע טעונה נסכים — אין סותר את כללו. וא"ת: ולמ"ד בריש איזהו מקומן (זבחים דף מט:) דכללו גמר מיניה — יהיו כל אשמות טעונות מתן בהונות, ולילפו נמי כולהו עריות מאשת אח? וי"ל: דלא גמר מיניה אלא דבר דלא חדש בו, כגון שחיטת צפון לעכב, אבל לענין חידוש לא גמר מיניה; כדפרש"י התם: דאם כן, היה יוצא לידון בדבר החדש כיוצא בו ללמד על הכלל כולו [ואין זה חידוש]:
Tosafot on Yevamot 7a:15:1.english: "Since the guilt-offering of a leper emerged to be judged by a new matter" - The fact that the sin-offering of a leper requires libations, whereas other sin-offerings do not require [them], is not considered a "new matter." And [a detail] is called a "new matter" only when it contradicts its general category: as [is the case] here, where other guilt-offerings require all of the blood [to be placed] on the altar, whereas for the leper's guilt-offering, [the priest] places from it on the thumbs and toes [of the leper]; and such as [the case of] a brother's wife, where all forbidden relations are prohibited, yet this one is permitted [for levirate marriage], which contradicts its general category. But the fact that the sin-offering of a leper requires libations does not contradict its general category. And if you say: According to the one who holds at the beginning of Eizehu Mekoman (Zevachim 49b) that its general category learns from it, should not all guilt-offerings require placement [of blood] on the thumbs and toes, and let all [other] forbidden relations also be derived from a brother's wife [to be permitted]? And one can say: [Its general category] learns from it only a matter in which it was not novel, such as slaughter in the north [being indispensable] to invalidate [the offering if omitted]; but regarding the novelty [itself], it does not learn from it, as Rashi explained there. For if so, it would be [a case of a matter that] emerged to be judged by a new matter akin to it to teach about the entire general category [and this would not be a novelty].

Tosafot on Yevamot 7a:1:1.hebrew: ומה עבודה שהיא חמורה ודוחה שבת רציחה דוחה אותה - הקשה הר"ר יעקב דאורלינ"ש: נימא "דיו"! מה רציחה אינו דוחה עבודה אלא בשב ואל תעשה, שבת נמי לא תדחה אלא בשב ואל תעשה? וי"ל, דאתיא כרבי טרפון, דאמר (ב"ק כה.): היכא דמיפרך ק"ו, לא אמרינן דיו. והא דאמר ליה ריש לקיש לר' יוחנן בפ' אחד דיני ממונות (סנהדרין דף לה.): "ותהא קבורת מת מצוה דוחה שבת מקל וחומר?" — לא משום דסבר כר"ט, אלא לא מסיק אדעתיה לחלק בין קום עשה לשב ואל תעשה, כי היכי דלא מסיק אדעתיה הש"ס בפ' מי שמתו (ברכות דף כ. ושם). ורבי יוחנן דלא מהדר ליה "דיו" — משום דמהדר ליה שפיר טפי: "רציחה תוכיח", דאפילו לרבי טרפון ליכא ק"ו. ועוד נראה לומר, דהכא דיינין הכי: ומה עבודה דקילא דחיא שבת, רציחה וקבורת מת מצוה דחמירא — לא כל שכן? ובמה הם חמורים? דעבודה נדחית מפניהם. ובפ' כיצד הרגל (ב"ק דף כה. ושם), דאמרו רבנן לר"ט "דיו", ולא דיינין: "ומה שן ורגל דקילי חייבים ברשות הניזק נזק שלם, קרן לא כ"ש?" — משום דאי נעביד קל וחומר הכי, איכא למפרך טובא, דאיכא בשן ורגל וליכא בקרן, כגון: יש הנאה להזיקן:
Tosafot on Yevamot 7a:1:1.english: "And if [the Temple] service, which is severe and overrides Shabbat, [the execution of a] murderer overrides it" - Rabbeinu Yaakov of Orléans raised a difficulty: Let us say [apply the principle of] dayyo ["it is sufficient"]: Just as [executing a] murderer does not override [the Temple] service except through [passive omission,] "sit and do not act" [shev ve'al ta'aseh], Shabbat, too, should not be overridden except through "sit and do not act"! And one can say that [this kal vachomer] follows Rabbi Tarfon, who said (Bava Kamma 25a): In a case where the kal vachomer would be nullified [by applying dayyo], we do not say dayyo. And that which Resh Lakish said to Rabbi Yochanan in the chapter [entitled] Echad Dinei Mamonot (Sanhedrin 35b): "And let the burial of a met mitzvah [an unattended corpse] override Shabbat by an a fortiori argument [kal vachomer]?" — [was] not because he holds in accordance with Rabbi Tarfon, but rather it did not occur to him [at first] to distinguish between [active commission,] "arise and act" [kum aseh], and [passive omission,] "sit and do not act" [shev ve'al ta'aseh], just as it did not occur to the Gemara in the chapter [entitled] Mi Shemeito (Berakhot 20a and there [in Tosafot]). And [as for the fact] that Rabbi Yochanan did not respond to him [with the refutation of] "dayyo" — [that is] because he gave him an even better response: "[The case of] murder will prove [otherwise]," for [with that refutation], even according to Rabbi Tarfon there is no kal vachomer. And furthermore, it appears [correct] to say that here we reason as follows: If [the Temple] service, which is lenient, overrides Shabbat, [the execution of a] murderer and the burial of a met mitzvah, which are stringent, is it not all the more so [that they should override Shabbat]? And in what [respect] are they stringent? In that [the Temple] service is overridden before them! And in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad HaRegel (Bava Kamma 25a and there [in Tosafot]), where the Rabbis said to Rabbi Tarfon "dayyo," and they did not reason: "If Shen [Tooth] and Regel [Foot], which are lenient, are liable for full damages in the domain of the injured party, is it not all the more so for Keren [Horn]?" — [that is] because if we were to construct the kal vachomer like that, there are many refutations [that could be raised, based on stringencies] that exist in Shen and Regel and do not exist in Keren, such as: there is pleasure in their damage.

Tosafot on Yevamot 7a:1:2.hebrew: שנאמר מעם מזבחי - ואפי' אם אין שם כהן אחר ראוי לעבודה, שהעבודה נדחית. וא"ת: ודלמא התם לאו משום דרציחה דחיא עבודה, אלא משום דגברא הוא דלא חזי? כדאמרי' (ברכות דף לב:): כהן שהרג נפש לא ישא את כפיו, שנאמר: "ידיכם דמים מלאו" — וכ"ש עבודה! וי"ל: דע"כ חזי, דאין מחלל עבודה, ד"מעם מזבחי" — ולא מעל מזבחי. ולא ישא את כפיו — חומרא בעלמא הוא. ועוד, דוקא לא ישא את כפיו לפי שהרגו בידו, ואין קטיגור נעשה סניגור, וכדכתיב בההוא קרא: "ובפרישכם כפיכם":
Tosafot on Yevamot 7a:1:2.english: "As it is stated: '[You shall take him] from My altar'" - And [this applies] even if there is no other priest there fit for the [Temple] service, such that the service is [indeed] overridden. And if you should say: But perhaps there, it is not because [the obligation to execute for] murder overrides the [Temple] service, but rather because the person [himself] is unfit [for the service]? As we say (Berakhot 32b): A priest who killed a person may not lift his hands [for the Priestly Blessing], as it is stated: "Your hands are full of blood" (Isaiah 1:15) — and all the more so [he should be disqualified from the Temple] service! And one can answer: Perforce he is fit, such that he does not profane the service, for [the Sages derive]: "From My altar" — but not from on top of My altar [i.e., if he has already begun the service atop the altar, he completes it, proving that his service is valid]. And [the rule that] he may not lift his hands is merely a stringency. And furthermore, it is specifically [that] he may not lift his hands because he killed with his hand, and an accuser cannot become an advocate — and as it is written in that [same] verse: "And when you spread your hands [I will hide My eyes from you... your hands are full of blood]" (Isaiah 1:15).

Tosafot on Yevamot 7a:3:1.hebrew: תלמוד לומר לא תבערו - וא"ת: אמאי איצטריך בפרק אחד דיני ממונות (סנהדרין דף לו.) מזבחי — המיוחד לי, למילף דרציחה דוחה אפילו קרבן צבור? תיפוק ליה מדאיצטריך לא תבערו לאפוקי מק"ו! ש"מ דרציחה דוחה אפי' קרבן צבור דדחי שבת, דאי קרבן יחיד — א"כ ליכא קל וחומר. וי"ל: דאי לאו דכתיב מזבחי, לא הוה מוקמינן קרא מסברא בקרבן צבור דכדי לדרוש לא תבערו לאפוקי מק"ו, אלא הוה מוקמינן קרא בקרבן יחיד, ולא תבערו הוה דרשינן ע"כ לשום דרשא אחריתי. א"נ: השתא דכתב לא תבערו, הוה מוקמינן קרא בקרבן יחיד מק"ו דאביי, דאמר בפ' אחד דיני ממונות (סנהדרין דף לה:): השתא דאמרת אין רציחה דוחה שבת, אין רציחה דוחה עבודה מק"ו — ומה שבת שנדחית מפני עבודה אין רציחה דוחה אותה, כו':
Tosafot on Yevamot 7a:3:1.english: "The verse states: 'You shall kindle no fire'" - And if you should say: Why was it necessary in the chapter [entitled] Echad Dinei Mamonot (Sanhedrin 36a) [to derive from the phrase] "from My altar" [that it refers to an offering] designated uniquely to Me, to learn that [the execution of a] murderer overrides even a communal offering? Let it be derived from [the fact] that "You shall kindle no fire" was necessary to exclude [execution from the] a fortiori inference [kal vachomer]; deduce from this that [the execution of a] murderer overrides even a communal offering, which overrides Shabbat, for if [it overrides only] an individual offering, if so, there is no a fortiori inference! And one can say: Were it not that "from My altar" is written, we would not establish the verse [based on] reasoning [alone] as referring to a communal offering, [merely] so that we could expound "You shall kindle no fire" to exclude [it] from an a fortiori inference; rather, we would establish the verse [as referring] to an individual offering, and "You shall kindle no fire" we would perforce expound for some other derivation. Alternatively: Now that [the Torah] wrote "You shall kindle no fire" [teaching that execution does not override Shabbat], we would establish the verse [as referring] to an individual offering, based on the a fortiori inference of Abaye, who said in the chapter [entitled] Echad Dinei Mamonot (Sanhedrin 35b): "Now that you say that [the execution of a] murderer does not override Shabbat, [the execution of a] murderer does not override the Temple service from an a fortiori inference: If Shabbat, which is overridden by the Temple service, is not overridden by [the execution of a] murderer, etc. [then the Temple service, which is not overridden by the Temple service, all the more so should not be overridden by it!]"
